deviations.what: Removed MESSAGE_TAGS from fairdm/conf/settings/apps.py, a file outside the story's scope, in its own commit (c3610f59).
deviations.why: Saving a profile redirects to the overview with a success message. The old Bootstrap-era tag 'success alert-success' reached django-mvp's alert as an icon name, so the overview raised IconNotFoundError for a person and for an organization. US1's tests stopped at the redirect and never opened that page, so scenario 2 (return to the page, told it was saved) could not hold. Two tests that follow the redirect fail without it. Revert that one commit if you would rather fix it elsewhere.

deviations.what: Replaced TestOrganizationIsEditableBy::test_nobody_may_edit_it_yet (US1) with the cases in T007, and changed two pre-existing organization checklist tests: test_every_management_action_is_disabled (now test_every_management_action_but_editing_is_disabled) and test_only_the_people_who_keep_the_record_are_offered_writing_its_description (a link, not a disabled button).
deviations.why: Each pinned a disabled organization stand-in that this story brings to life, which tasks.md allows. Named in progress.md under T007 and T010.

deviations.what: The three seeded accounts are in a new PROFILE_ACCOUNTS tuple, not in EXAMPLE_ACCOUNTS; demo/seed/common.py gained create_accounts() and profile_accounts().
deviations.why: EXAMPLE_ACCOUNTS is created by every seed through example_accounts(), and the docs say seed_overviews creates three accounts. EXAMPLE_ACCOUNT_EMAILS includes both tuples, so fairdm.E501 reports the new addresses. The docs check requires create_accounts to be documented, so overview-pages.md names it.

deviations.what: The parent field uses the package's django-autocomplete-light organization picker, which searches every organization including the one being edited.
deviations.why: The picker AffiliationForm already uses fits a single parent. Narrowing the queryset would turn the loop refusal into a generic 'not a valid choice' instead of the reason on the field.

concerns: An organization whose stored ROR identifier is the full address (https://ror.org/...) cannot be saved from the editing page. Organization.clean matches stored ROR values against ^0[a-z0-9]{6}[0-9]{2}$, the bare identifier, but Organization.update_identifier stores synced_data['id'], which ROR gives as the full address. I confirmed full_clean fails on such a record while a bare identifier passes. With T018 the owner sees a form-level error instead of a server error, but still cannot save. The seeded organizations use bare identifiers and are not affected. The model's check is outside this story; accepting the address or normalising the stored value is the model's to settle (decisions D18).

PersonProfileForm.__init__ (forms/profile.py, US1) reads self.fields['lang'] unconditionally, so a portal form that leaves 'lang' out of Meta.fields, as contributors.md says a portal may do to drop a field, raises KeyError: 'lang' when the form is built. I ran a subclass with fields = ['name', 'profile'] to confirm it. Other dropped fields work: the shipped form drops them from the page. I left it alone, it is US1's code.
The parent picker offers the organization itself; the refusal is shown after submitting, not prevented in the list (decisions D15).
